findings.limits: The group is actually clean in this counterexample. This establishes a protocol/trust success-gate failure, not an observed surviving writer or a claim that a Linux deadline actually fired.
findings.minimal_fix: Success must require exact-int keeper_returncode0, lease_released is True, intentional group KILL not used, valid no-live cleanup and matching original control PID/inner returncode, while preserving all existing timeout/resource/clock guards. Add the real after-release keeper death regression. Timeout/failed cleanup receipts may truthfully report group emptiness but cannot become success.
findings.reproduced: A real local owned inner returns0/control; parent really flushes R, then the fixture SIGKILLs only that owned keeper. Return receipt has keeper_returncode=-9, lease_released=true, no live members and cleanup_error=null. Exact command_ok accepts it.
findings.title: Abnormal keeper termination after release is accepted as command success

findings.limits: This is a reproducible evidence-custody gap, not a fail-open inventory decision. The ps response is an explicit LOCAL fault provider; no false claim of a real host ps UTF8 fault is made.
findings.minimal_fix: Capture every bounded ps response/exception stdout/stderr/timeout prefix losslessly with SHA/bytes/base64 and parse_error before checks; retain each inventory attempt in the final command receipt even when parse, nonzero status or timeout fails. Preserve original error and existing budget/ownership checks.
findings.reproduced: An explicit first ps response contains non-UTF8 original stdout and stderr. _members raises while run_owned retains only UnicodeDecodeError text; neither original stream is present in the returned receipt, and there is no per-attempt inventory response list. Later real scans clean the owned group and eligibility correctly remains failed.
findings.title: Inventory parse/timeout/nonzero failure loses original ps bytes and attempt evidence
